docs.title: HELHEST dataset_tools
docs.text:
dataset_tools converts recordings from the HELHEST robot (ROS 2 bags) into a flat, machine-learning-ready dataset. Each finished scene contains synchronised camera frames, deskewed lidar clouds in the robot's base frame, odometry, gravity alignment, height maps, and proprioception. The repository also builds root-level release files and provides a web viewer for inspecting a finished root.

Bags are read with the pure-Python rosbags library, so you do not need a ROS installation.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e .                  # Python >= 3.12
.venv/bin/helhest-extract  /path/to/bags /path/to/root --jobs 8     # one scene per bag: 0000/, 0001/, ...
.venv/bin/helhest-validate /path/to/root --csv /path/to/root/validation.csv

uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-viewer && uv pip install --python .venv-viewer -e ".[viewer]"
.venv-viewer/bin/helhest-viewer /path/to/root --open                # http://127.0.0.1:8080/

The viewer line requires uv (see Installation for the pip route).

This workflow produces a bare root: scenes containing clouds, images, and poses. A complete release root also includes height maps, keyframe lists, and a manifest; see Building a release root.

docs.title: Building a release root
docs.text:
A release root is built entirely using tools in this repository, in two stages. The first stage operates per bag: extracting the data, rotating odometry into the cloud coordinate frame, generating height maps, and validating each scene. The second stage operates on the whole root: producing the manifest, dataset splits, keyframe lists, README, full validation report, and atlas.

The steps below use the Slurm jobs in slurm/ on the CTU RCI cluster. The same steps without Slurm follow at the end.

docs.title: 1. Describe the release
docs.text:
A release is described by two tracked files in docs/. These files live in the repository, not on this site:

The bag list, docs/v2_<n>_bags.csv (e.g. docs/v2_4_bags.csv): one row per scene, in scene order, with the header

scene,session,bag_dir_on_subtdata,bag_size_gb,bag_start_utc,duration_s,lidar_msgs,camera_msgs[,extract_args]

The jobs parse columns by position, so scene must be the first column and the bag directory the third. The optional extract_args column holds extractor options for that bag alone, such as --trim_idle 60 10. Bag lists are cumulative: each release lists every scene in its root, including those from earlier releases. The jobs split rows on raw commas (not quoted CSV), so no field, extract_args included, may contain a comma.

The spec, docs/releases/v2_<n>.json:

  • Required: dataset_version, bags (the list above, relative to the repository root) and held_out.scenes.
  • Optional: inherit (a spec to merge under this one; helhest_v2.json holds text shared across releases for this rig), title, summary, held_out.decision and extra held_out keys (e.g. held_out.support), bag_host, images, corrections, sessions, excluded, terrain_notes, defects, open_items and curation (becomes atlas/curation.json).

Use docs/releases/v2_4.json as a template. The spec's descriptive blocks (rig, camera, gps, odometry, sessions, ...) and bag_host, images, corrections and held_out are copied or merged into the manifest; everything else is measured from the scenes.

docs.title: 2. Extract every bag
docs.text:
From the repository root on a login node, with .venv built inside the container (see Installation), and key-based ssh from the cluster to subtdata: each task rsyncs its bag from $SUBTDATA (default $USER@subtdata.felk.cvut.cz). EXTRACT_ARGS adds extractor options to every task of a submission, after the row's own extract_args.

mkdir -p slurm/slurm_out
CSV=docs/v2_4_bags.csv HM_ARGS="--set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none" \
    sbatch --array=0-35%4 slurm/extract_v2.batch /mnt/personal/$USER/HELHEST_v2_4

The array range covers the rows of the bag list (0 to rows - 1); %4 caps how many jobs run at once. CSV= and the root are required. HM_ARGS sets the height-map settings; the tool's defaults are not v2.4's, so a v2.4 build passes the p90 settings shown. A root that links in an earlier release's scenes is submitted with the range of its new rows only.

Each array task produces one finished scene:

  1. copies its bag with rsync from subtdata to node-local scratch;
  2. runs helhest-extract on it, with the row's extract_args;
  3. runs helhest-odom-frame measure, then apply if the measurement succeeded (a scene it cannot measure keeps the Odin1's own odometry and gravity alignment, with a warning);
  4. runs helhest-heightmap with HM_ARGS;
  5. validates the scene, moves it into <root>/<scene>/, and writes the report to <root>/.validation/<scene>.csv.

A task skips a scene whose source_bag.txt already names the same bag, so resubmitting the same range resumes. The job checks only that file, not the frame counts. A scene that holds a different bag stops the task. FORCE=1 re-extracts the scene in both cases. A scene that fails validation is not published unless FORCE_PUBLISH=1 is set. The exit code names the failing step:

Exit code Step 10 fetching the bag 11 extraction 12 publishing the scene 13 the scene holds a different bag 14 validation 15 the odometry-frame rotation (apply) 16 the height maps

Logs go to slurm/slurm_out/. SIF and REPO override the container image and the checkout; slurm/README.md lists every site-specific value.

docs.title: 3. Finalise the root
docs.text:
On the login node, not through sbatch:

slurm/finalize_v2.sh /mnt/personal/$USER/HELHEST_v2_4 docs/v2_4_bags.csv docs/releases/v2_4.json

This runs helhest-release (root-level files), validates the whole root into <root>/validation.csv, and draws the viewer's atlas with scripts/make_atlas.py. It exits 2 if helhest-release fails; otherwise with the validation step's exit code. Atlas problems are logged but do not change the exit code. The spec (third argument) is optional: without it the script only rewrites scenes.csv and declares the image format, with no manifest or keyframe lists.

docs.title: 4. Check it
docs.text:
helhest-validate <root> -v           # include INFO findings
helhest-disk-usage <root> --all     # rescan every scene for the viewer
helhest-viewer <root> --open         # look at it

docs.title: Without Slurm
docs.text:
Extract one bag per bag-list row, each with --start_index set to its scene number and that row's extract_args (bags fetched into one local directory <bags>, keeping their directory names):

tail -n +2 docs/v2_4_bags.csv | while IFS=, read -r scene _ bag _ _ _ _ _ args; do
    helhest-extract "<bags>/$(basename "$bag")" <root> --start_index "$((10#$scene))" $args
done
helhest-odom-frame measure <root> --fits fits.json
helhest-odom-frame apply   <root> --fits fits.json
helhest-heightmap <root> --set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none
helhest-release   <root> --spec docs/releases/v2_4.json
helhest-validate  <root> --csv <root>/validation.csv
.venv/bin/python scripts/make_atlas.py <root> --bags docs/v2_4_bags.csv

Run helhest-odom-frame before helhest-heightmap, because apply rotates gravity_align.npy, which the height maps are levelled with; if odom-frame is re-run on a scene that already has maps, rebuild them with --overwrite.

docs.title: Rebuilding only the height maps
docs.text:
After a root's clouds or gravity_align.npy change:

HM_ARGS="--set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none" \
    sbatch --array=0-35 slurm/heightmaps.batch /mnt/personal/$USER/HELHEST_v2_4   # array index = scene
helhest-heightmap <root> --scenes 0003 --overwrite                            # or by hand

The batch job first checks a sample of the existing maps against a rebuild (VERIFY=0 skips this) and passes HM_ARGS through to helhest-heightmap. The tool's defaults are not the settings v2.4 was built with; v2.4's maps use statistic=p90 and no tie jitter, so pass HM_ARGS="--set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none" to the batch job and --set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none by hand. Each scene's height_maps.json records the settings it was built with. --scenes takes comma-separated scene directory names, e.g. 0003,0004. The tool will not write through a scene whose height maps are linked from another root; build them in the root that owns them.

docs.title: Dataset layout
docs.text: HELHEST is a small three-wheeled skid-steer field robot built at CTU in Prague (VRAS group). It carries a Manifold Tech Odin1 lidar-camera-IMU unit and a Fixposition GNSS/INS, plus wheel encoders. A HELHEST root holds one directory per recording (scene), with every per-frame file index-aligned, alongside root-level metadata files.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
Sensor Topic In a scene as Odin1 lidar, 256 x 192 raster at ~14.4 Hz /odin1/cloud_filtered/cloudini clouds/, in base_link Odin1 camera, 1600 x 1296, fisheye /odin1/image/compressed images/, camera_info.yaml, T_cam_to_base.txt Odin1 lidar-inertial odometry, 14.4 Hz, 6-DoF /odin1/odometry odometry.txt, transforms.npy, gravity_align.npy Odin1 IMU, 400 Hz /odin1/imu used to deskew the sweeps Fixposition GNSS/INS /fixposition/odometry_llh, /fixposition/odometry_enu gps.npy, and the check in pose_check.txt Wheels /joint_states, /joint_setpoints, /cmd_vel joint_states.npy, joint_setpoints.npy, cmd_vel.npy

Camera and lidar run 1:1 at about 14.4 Hz, so a scene has about 14.4 frames per second.

docs.title: Root layout
docs.text:
<root>/
├── 0000/ … 0035/            one directory per scene
├── manifest.json            what the release is: version, scenes, sessions, held-out scenes, defects
├── splits.json              train / validation split
├── scenes.csv               scene, bag, start time, frame count
├── keyframes.lst            usable frames of every scene
├── keyframes_train.lst      ... of the training scenes
├── keyframes_heldout.lst    ... of the held-out scenes
├── README.md                the release described in prose
├── validation.csv           helhest-validate's report
├── disk_usage.json          sizes per scene and modality
├── atlas/                   the viewer's curated index and thumbnails
└── listings/                optional: per-scene file lists for viewers opening the root by URL

The held-out scenes are listed in manifest.json under held_out.scenes. A loader that trains on a root must keep them out of every training fold; the provided keyframe lists (keyframes_train.lst) already exclude them.

docs.title: Scene files
docs.text: F is the number of frames in the scene. Every per-frame file and every (F, ...) array is index-aligned: images/00042.jpg, clouds/00042.npy, data_ts[42], transforms[42], and gravity_align[42] all describe the exact same instant.

docs.title: Per frame
docs.text:
Path Shape, dtype Content images/NNNNN.jpg JPEG, 1600 x 1296 the camera's raw compressed JPEG bytes, unmodified clouds/NNNNN.npy (N, 4) float32 x, y, z in metres and intensity, in base_link, deskewed onto the frame's instant. N varies; NaN and all-zero points are dropped. The robot's own body reflections are retained height_maps/NNNNN.npz 128 x 128 float64, key height_map terrain height in metres, gravity-aligned base frame, 0.1 m cells, ±6.4 m. Rows correspond to x forward, columns to y left height_masks/NNNNN.npz 128 x 128 uint8, key validity source of each cell's height: 0 extrapolated, 1 interpolated, 2 measured, 3 wheel contact data_ts.txt (F,) the frame's instant, Unix seconds pcd_ts.txt (F,) the lidar timestamp, on the same latency-corrected clock transforms.npy (F, 4, 4) float64 base pose per frame relative to frame 0, interpolated from odometry. One track for the whole scene, not split at segment breaks (see Ground truth) gravity_align.npy (F, 3, 3) float64 Ry(pitch) @ Rx(roll) of the base: applied to a cloud (pts @ R.T), it levels the ground. Yaw is omitted

A frame with too few lidar returns produces no height map. HELHEST v2.4's height maps are built with the p90 cell statistic and no tie jitter; each scene's height_maps.json records the exact settings.

docs.title: Per scene
docs.text:
Files fed by a topic or TF the bag lacks are not written; odometry.txt and its segment table need ground truth enabled (the default for the Odin1).

Path Content odometry.txt ground truth: base poses at the odometry's full rate within the kept segments; one row per pose with 17 values, the timestamp followed by the row-major 4 x 4 matrix odometry_segments.txt segment table for odometry.txt; see Ground truth camera_info.yaml full camera calibration: resolution, distortion model and coefficients, K, R, and P camera_intrinsics.txt the 3 x 3 intrinsic matrix K T_cam_to_base.txt 4 x 4 extrinsic transform: p_base = T @ p_cam_optical joint_states.npy (M, 1 + 3J): timestamp, followed by positions, velocities, and efforts of the J wheels at full rate (not frame-aligned) joint_names.txt wheel joint names matching the column order in joint_states.npy joint_setpoints.npy commanded wheel states with the same layout as joint_states.npy, where recorded cmd_vel.npy (M, 7): timestamp, linear and angular velocity in the base frame, where recorded gps.npy (M, 8): timestamp, latitude, longitude, altitude, fix status, and east, north, and up variances (not frame-aligned)

docs.title: Extraction records
docs.text:
These describe how the scene was generated and provide provenance. They are the first place to look when something in a scene seems wrong.

Path Content extract_meta.json the extraction run (git commit, all options), the source bag (topics and message counts), all streams with data gaps exceeding 1 s, and frame filtering records source_bag.txt the bag the scene originated from; also serves as the completion sentinel for the scene time_align.txt the estimated publish latency subtracted from the frame clock pose_check.txt odometry compared against the Fixposition at base_link: jumps, displacement disagreement over 1, 2, and 5 s, clock lag, and tilt (at the child frame when TF does not reach base_link) gnss_guard.txt frames and poses the guard removed: fabricated-pose spans and frames without a bracketing pose tf_pins.txt fixed extrinsics used by the scene compared against what the bag itself published odom_frame.txt the rotation applied to odometry by helhest-odom-frame height_maps.json the configuration settings used to build height maps

docs.title: Coordinate frames
docs.text:
• base_link: x forward, y left, z up, at the robot base. Clouds, poses, and height maps are all expressed in this frame.
  • Camera: T_cam_to_base.txt maps points from the camera's optical frame (x right, y down, z forward) to base_link. The camera is a fisheye (equidistant model in camera_info.yaml), so undistort before projecting.
  • Gravity: gravity_align.npy holds the base's roll and pitch per frame. It is the only source of absolute attitude in a scene.
  • Earth: gps.npy is the only georeference. It is intended for mapping and comparison, not ground truth.

docs.title: Ground truth
docs.text:
odometry.txt is the Odin1's lidar-inertial odometry, expressed at base_link. It is split into segments, listed in odometry_segments.txt, which are numbered from 1. Each segment starts at the identity pose at its first sample and runs from there. For each segment, the table gives its time span, its pose count, and why it ended:

Reason Meaning gap the odometry was silent for more than 1 s teleport a jump faster than 6 m/s, such as the Odin1 relocalising fix_lost the pose source had no valid solution end_of_run the recording ended

Segments shorter than 20 poses are dropped and appear in neither file.

Never bridge two segments. Within a segment, compute relative motion with inv(T0) @ Ti. A segment's frame is defined by the robot's attitude at its first pose and is therefore not guaranteed to be level (z is up only if the robot started level): obtain absolute roll and pitch from gravity_align.npy.

transforms.npy is the same odometry sampled at each frame, but as one unsegmented track anchored at frame 0. Do not take pose differences across a segment boundary: assign frames to segments with the time spans in odometry_segments.txt. Within the odometry, poses are interpolated; across a gap or a teleport the nearest pose is used instead. Frames the odometry does not cover are dropped by default (--gnss_guard).

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
data_ts.txt is the instant every per-frame file of that frame describes:

  • The publish latency is removed. The Odin1 stamps some messages upon publish rather than capture, with a delay that varies under load. The extractor measures this delay per scene and subtracts it (time_align.txt).
  • Clouds are deskewed. The Odin1 scans its raster from bottom to top over 67 ms. Every return is moved to where the robot was at data_ts, using the odometry and the IMU, so a cloud is a snapshot at the exact instant of its camera image. Sweeps without per-point times or odometry around them are written as recorded and counted in extract_meta.json.

Full-rate streams (odometry.txt within its segments, joint_states.npy, gps.npy, ...) carry their own timestamps on the same Unix clock.

docs.title: Recordings
docs.text:
The current release, HELHEST v2.4, holds 36 scenes from seven sessions in September and October 2026:

Scenes Date Site 0000-0001 2026-09-14 Stromovka park, Prague: Robotour test runs on cobbles, gravel and asphalt 0002 2026-09-19 Stromovka park: the Robotour 2026 finals, driven autonomously 0003-0006 2026-09-22 Lipník nad Bečvou army UGV polygon: ploughed field, mud, banks, ballast 0007-0015 2026-09-28 Temešvár: tall-grass meadow, sprints, wheel-slip tests, two roll-overs, forest track 0016-0021 2026-09-29 Temešvár: the same meadow, late afternoon into dusk 0022-0028 2026-10-02 Temešvár: pine and mixed forest, the meadow 0029-0035 2026-10-07 Stromovka park, off the paths: lawn, woodland, tall weeds

The held-out (validation) scenes are 0001, 0019, 0020, 0024, 0025, 0026, 0027, 0034 and 0035, one per kind of ground, each on ground the training scenes do not drive.

manifest.json lists each session, the held-out scenes, and the known defects of every scene.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The tools require Python 3.12 or newer. Installation is split into two environments: one for the extraction tools and one for the viewer. Keep them separate because the viewer depends on PyTorch (torch), which the extraction tools never use.

docs.title: Extraction tools
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e .

This installs every helhest-* command except the viewer. The base dependencies are rosbags, numpy, opencv-python-headless, and scipy.

Optional extras:

Extra Adds Needed for build open3d helhest-odom-frame measure (part of building a release root). The Linux wheel requires glibc 2.29 or newer. test pytest, httpx Running the test suite viewer FastAPI, uvicorn, Jinja2, SimView, torch helhest-viewer (see below)

docs.title: Viewer
docs.text:
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-viewer
uv pip install --python .venv-viewer -e ".[viewer]"

On Linux, uv installs torch from the CPU-only index configured in pyproject.toml; on macOS it uses the regular PyPI wheel. Plain pip ignores that configuration and on Linux downloads the CUDA build (about 3 GB); with pip, install the CPU build first:

python3 -m venv .venv-viewer
.venv-viewer/bin/pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
.venv-viewer/bin/pip install -e ".[viewer]"

The viewer requires SimView 6.1.1 or newer and refuses to start with earlier versions.

docs.title: Container (CTU RCI cluster)
docs.text:
On the cluster, create the virtual environment using the container's Python interpreter and run all commands through the container. Network data shares are not mounted inside the container by default, so always specify --bind:

SIF=/mnt/data/vras/data/helhest-jazzy.sif
singularity exec --bind /mnt/personal --bind /mnt/data $SIF python3 -m venv .venv
singularity exec --bind /mnt/personal --bind /mnt/data $SIF .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[build]"
singularity exec --bind /mnt/personal --bind /mnt/data $SIF \
    .venv/bin/helhest-extract <bags> <root> --jobs 8

Add --bind for any other filesystem you read from or write to. The extraction, height-map and finalize jobs in slurm/ expect a virtual environment built this way at <repository>/.venv; slurm/viewer.batch expects the viewer environment at <repository>/.venv-viewer.

docs.title: The cloudini decoder
docs.text:
The Odin1 lidar publishes compressed clouds (cloudini). The decoder ships prebuilt at dataset_tools/libcloudini_shim.so and was built on Ubuntu 22.04 and needs glibc 2.32 or newer (GLIBC_2.32, GLIBCXX_3.4.30). On older systems, rebuild it once:

cloudini_shim/build_shim.sh

This requires cmake and a C++20-capable g++. build_shim.sh clones the cloudini sources from GitHub unless an existing checkout is passed as its first argument (cloudini_shim/build_shim.sh <cloudini-checkout>), so it needs git and network access otherwise; it uses system zstd/lz4 headers when present, else builds vendored copies. All prerequisites are available in helhest-jazzy.sif, so if in doubt, run the script inside the container.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Every tool is a command installed with the package. Run any of them with --help for the full list of options.

Command What it does helhest-extract Extracts ROS 2 bags into scene directories helhest-odom-frame Aligns odometry with the lidar cloud coordinate frame helhest-heightmap Generates height maps and validity masks from a scene's clouds helhest-keyframes Generates keyframe lists for a root helhest-release Generates root-level release files from a specification helhest-validate Validates scenes and complete roots helhest-viewer Browses a root in a web browser helhest-disk-usage Summarises disk usage per scene and modality helhest-image-format Declares or checks the image format stored in a root helhest-sort-bag Rewrites a bag sorted by header timestamp

docs.title: helhest-extract
docs.text:
Extracts ROS 2 bags into scene directories (0000/, 0001/, etc.), producing one scene per bag. See the dataset layout for details on all generated files.

helhest-extract <dir-with-bags> <root> --jobs 8

<dir-with-bags> can be a directory containing multiple bags or a single bag directory. Only directories containing metadata.yaml are recognised as bags. Scenes are numbered sequentially according to the sorted names of the bag directories.

By default, the extractor reads the robot's primary sensors: the Odin1 lidar-camera unit and the Fixposition GNSS/INS. Spelled out in full, the default arguments are:

--cam /odin1/image/compressed --lidar /odin1/cloud_filtered/cloudini \
--odom /odin1/odometry --imu /odin1/odometry --deskew_imu /odin1/imu \
--check_odom /fixposition/odometry_enu --gps auto

Processing pipeline. Camera and lidar frames are matched by mutual nearest neighbour on their header timestamps, and unpaired frames are dropped. Each lidar sweep that carries per-point times and is bracketed by odometry is deskewed to its frame's instant; other sweeps are written as recorded and counted in extract_meta.json. Odometry is interpolated onto each frame. With --time_align auto, the publish latency is then measured from the written clouds and subtracted from the frame clock. See Timing in the dataset layout for clock details.

Resuming. A scene counts as complete when source_bag.txt, written last, is present and its image, cloud and timestamp counts agree. Completed scenes are skipped by default, allowing an interrupted run to be resumed cleanly; --overwrite re-extracts them. If an existing scene corresponds to a different bag than expected, the run stops before extracting anything (exit code 2) to prevent indexing conflicts from an altered bag list.

Failures. If a bag fails, its traceback is logged and the run continues with remaining bags. The summary at the end lists every failed and empty scene, and the command exits with code 1 if any bag failed. It exits with 2 when no bag is found, --scenes selects none, or an existing scene holds a different bag.

docs.title: Main options
docs.text:
Option Meaning --jobs N Number of worker processes, processing one bag each (default: 4; 1 runs in-process) --scenes 0 3 5-9 <bag-name> Extract only specified scene indices, ranges, or bag directory names --start_index N Number the first scene N instead of 0000 --overwrite Re-extract scenes that are already complete --base_frame Target coordinate frame for clouds, odometry, and gravity alignment (default: base_link) --gt auto/on/off Write ground-truth odometry.txt and odometry_segments.txt (auto: enables this for Odin1 and Fixposition odometry) --time_align auto/off/S Correct frame timestamps for publish latency: measured per scene (auto, default), fixed duration in seconds, or disabled (off) --deskew auto/off Motion-compensate each lidar return to the robot's pose at the frame timestamp, where the sweep has per-point times and odometry covers it (default: auto) --deskew_imu TOPIC IMU topic providing angular velocity for intra-sweep deskewing (default: /odin1/imu; off interpolates poses instead) --imu TOPIC Orientation source for gravity_align.npy (default: /odin1/odometry) --check_odom TOPIC Reference odometry stream compared against primary odometry in pose_check.txt (default: /fixposition/odometry_enu; off skips) --gnss_guard auto/on/off Drop frames the pose stream does not cover and stretches of transient GNSS/INS reset solutions. auto (default) runs the full guard for Fixposition odometry, the coverage-only part for /odin1/odometry; recorded in gnss_guard.txt --trim_idle MAX_S KEEP_S Cut every stop (odometry under 0.15 m/s and 5 deg/s) longer than MAX_S seconds to its first KEEP_S seconds of frames; odometry.txt is kept whole (off by default) --gps TOPIC GNSS fix topic for gps.npy; auto (default) selects the active NavSatFix topic, off records none --tf_pins on/off Replace online Odin1 lidar and camera extrinsic estimates (which drift across and within bags) with one constant: the median of what 42 bags published (default: on) --lidar_extrinsic X Y Z ROLL PITCH YAW Fixed lidar-to-base transform when unavailable from the TF tree, in metres and radians --allow_frame_fallback Extract even when TF does not reach --base_frame, leaving that stream in its native frame (otherwise the scene fails) --max_sync_dt S Maximum allowable timestamp difference between synchronised camera and lidar frames (default: 0.1) --cam_time_offset S Seconds added to the camera stamps before pairing; unlike --time_align, this changes which camera and lidar frames are paired (default: 0) --image_format camera/png Store raw compressed JPEG bytes from the camera (default) or decode to PNG -v Enable verbose/debug logging

All options used during extraction, along with automatic decisions, are recorded in each scene's extract_meta.json.

Preserving derived files on re-extraction. Height maps and other derived products are built after extraction. If a re-extraction produces the same data_ts.txt, they are kept. If the timestamps differ, each derived directory (height_maps/, height_masks/, proprio_labels/, driven_similarity/) and height_maps.json is renamed whole to <name>.stale-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS, so no product is left misaligned with the new frames.

docs.title: Caveats of the raw bags
docs.text:
• Publish latency. The Odin1 stamps some messages on publish rather than capture; on the 2026-09 recordings the poses run ahead of the images and clouds by up to about 0.69 s, varying with load within one bag. --time_align auto measures and removes it per scene (time_align.txt).
  • A GNSS/INS without a fix keeps publishing. After a roll-over the Fixposition can fill its odometry with a reset state hundreds of metres away and no flag. --gnss_guard drops such stretches (gnss_guard.txt, fix_lost in odometry_segments.txt).
  • The Odin1 re-estimates its own extrinsics on /tf_static, drifting across and within bags. --tf_pins (default) replaces them with one constant.
  • /imu/data is mounted tilted and has no TF to base_link: do not pass it as --imu.
  • The 2026-08 bags are not dataset material. Their TF tree lacks the base_link -> odin1_base_link edge, so a scene fails unless --lidar_extrinsic or --allow_frame_fallback is given.

docs/EXTRACTION_GUARDS.md in the repository explains how the latency and GNSS guards decide.

docs.title: helhest-odom-frame
docs.text:
The Odin1 computes its odometry with an online estimate of the lidar-to-IMU extrinsic. The clouds use the fixed value --tf_pins sets. Consequently, a scene's odometry frame and cloud frame can differ by up to 0.8 degrees. This tool measures that angular offset by registering clouds against each other (ICP) and rotates odometry.txt, transforms.npy, and gravity_align.npy into the cloud frame. Only measure needs the build extra. Both subcommands take --scenes. apply refuses a scene that already has odom_frame.txt or a correction over 3 degrees. After apply, rebuild the scene's height maps and the keyframe lists.

helhest-odom-frame measure <root> --fits fits.json   # every scene with clouds and no odom_frame.txt
helhest-odom-frame apply   <root> --fits fits.json

The result is recorded in each scene's odom_frame.txt. Re-extracting a scene removes this file, so rerun measure and apply afterwards.

docs.title: helhest-heightmap
docs.text:
Builds a height map and validity mask for each frame. The cloud is levelled using gravity_align.npy and binned onto a 128 x 128 grid of 0.1 m cells around base_link, then interpolated, filled, and smoothed.

helhest-heightmap <root>                           # every scene
helhest-heightmap <root> --scenes 0003 --overwrite    # rebuild one scene
helhest-heightmap <root> --workers 16 --set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none

The parameters used are recorded in each scene's height_maps.json. The tool's defaults are not the settings HELHEST v2.4 was built with: v2.4's maps use --set statistic=p90 --set tie_jitter=none. Frames that already have a map are kept unless --overwrite is passed; adding maps with different settings to a scene is refused, so rebuild the whole scene with --overwrite. Frames with too few lidar returns receive no map.

docs.title: helhest-keyframes
docs.text:
Writes the root's three keyframe lists: keyframes.lst (all scenes), keyframes_train.lst (training scenes), and keyframes_heldout.lst (held-out scenes). Each line lists one frame that contains a cloud, an image, a height map, and a mask:

0003/clouds/00042.npy 0003/images/00042.jpg

Frames tilted more than 45 degrees, and the 4 s before such a tilt, are excluded (--max_tilt_deg, --tilt_horizon; a negative --max_tilt_deg disables the gate). --out_dir writes the lists elsewhere. Held-out scenes are determined from manifest.json. The image extension comes from manifest.json (images.extension). helhest-release runs this step automatically.

docs.title: helhest-release
docs.text:
Generates a release's root-level files from its specification and scenes: scenes.csv, the keyframe lists, manifest.json, splits.json, atlas/curation.json, and README.md.

helhest-release <root> --spec docs/releases/v2_4.json
helhest-release <root> --spec docs/releases/v2_4.json --out_dir /tmp/compare

With --out_dir, the files go to that directory, except scenes.csv, which is only updated in the root itself.

The specification holds curated metadata that cannot be derived automatically: the bag list, held-out scene selections and rationales, session groupings, and known defects. The spec's descriptive blocks and keys such as bag_host, images and corrections are copied or merged into the manifest; everything else is measured from the scenes. The tool rejects a root whose scene directories do not match the bag list (a missing, extra or mismatched scene), or where a designated held-out scene is missing from disk. See Building a release root.

docs.title: helhest-validate
docs.text:
Validates extracted scenes and prints a diagnostic report.

helhest-validate <root>                                # a whole root
helhest-validate <root>/0000 <root>/0001               # single scenes
helhest-validate <root> --csv <root>/validation.csv    # the report the viewer shows
helhest-validate <root> --json <root>/validation.json --strict

The validator verifies that required files are present, that frame counts agree across images, clouds, timestamps, poses, and gravity alignment, that timestamps are monotonic, that a sample of clouds (8 per scene, --sample-clouds N, 0 skips them) has the expected (N, 4) shape and a consistent float dtype, that rotation matrices are valid, and that camera calibration parameters and extrinsics are reasonable. It also checks ground-truth segments, proprioception and GNSS streams, per-frame products, and, for a whole root, the manifest and keyframe lists.

Findings are reported at three severity levels:

  • ERROR: Structural defects. Exit code 1.
  • WARN: Data-quality issues, such as NaNs, implausible speeds, or extreme tilt. Passing --strict causes warnings to fail with exit code 1 as well.
  • INFO: Informational notices that do not indicate defects, such as a gap in the frame clock. Displayed with -v.

Exit code 2 means a path was not found or the expect file is unreadable.

Every finding has a stable identifier printed in brackets. To use --strict on a root with known acceptable anomalies, list them in <root>/validation_expect.json:

{"expected": [["0008", "TILT"], ["*", "CLOUD_EMPTY"]]}

Expected findings no longer fail the run; they stay in --json output and are printed with -v. An entry that matches nothing is reported as an INFO finding EXPECT_UNUSED (shown with -v), so stale exceptions are noticed. --expect PATH reads another file.

docs.title: helhest-disk-usage
docs.text:
Generates <root>/disk_usage.json, recording bytes and file counts per scene and modality for the viewer's disk-usage panels. It scans only scenes not yet present in the file, unless scenes are specified explicitly or --all is passed. Use --all to refresh sizes after a scene changed. Extraction runs update this file automatically for the scenes they process.

helhest-disk-usage <root> [scene ...] [--all]

docs.title: helhest-image-format
docs.text:
Declares in manifest.json whether a root stores raw camera JPEG bytes or PNG images. Any scene containing images in a format different from the declared one is reported as an error. helhest-extract runs the declaration at the end of every run, so manifest.json can exist before the release step. A JPEG root is declared as images.extension: jpg; a root without the declaration is read as PNG. Both modes exit 1 when the scenes do not hold one format or disagree with the declaration.

helhest-image-format <root>            # declare what the scenes hold
helhest-image-format <root> --check    # report only

docs.title: helhest-sort-bag
docs.text:
Rewrites a bag with its messages sorted by header timestamp; messages without a usable header stamp keep their bag receive time. The extractor already sorts timestamps before pairing frames, so this tool is rarely needed. The entire bag is loaded into memory during sorting. An existing output is refused unless --overwrite is passed.

helhest-sort-bag <input-bag> <output-bag> [--overwrite]

docs.title: Viewer
docs.text:
helhest-viewer serves a web view of a dataset root: an index of every scene and its contents, a page per scene with its validation findings, trajectory map, and signals over time, a per-frame inspection view, and an interactive 3D view of each odometry segment showing the terrain, aggregated cloud, robot poses, and camera. The 3D view is built on SimView.

The viewer operates in read-only mode on scene data. The only files it writes to a root are reviewer notes in <root>/notes/. It requires only the scene directories to run: scenes lacking optional files will still open, with missing files indicated.

Install the viewer as described under Installation.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
helhest-viewer /path/to/root --open                          # serves http://127.0.0.1:8080/
helhest-viewer http://subtdata.felk.cvut.cz/HELHEST/ --open  # a root published on a web server

When a root is provided as a URL, files are mirrored into the local cache as you browse, and reviewer notes default to <cache-dir>/notes. scripts/viewer_public.sh [viewer flags] starts the viewer on the public release and opens a browser; VIEWER_URL points it at another root.

Option Default Meaning --host, --port 127.0.0.1, 8080 address and port to listen on --uds PATH off listen on a Unix socket instead, in a directory with restricted permissions; reach it with ssh -L 8080:PATH host (--open has no effect with it) --max-seconds, --max-frames 600, 12000 split segments longer than this into equal viewing windows --cache-dir ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/dataset_tools_viewer/<root-name>-<hash> directory for cached probes, built 3D windows and a URL root's mirror --cache-max-gb 5.0 size limit for the built 3D windows in gigabytes; least recently used windows are evicted first --clear-cache empty this root's cache (probes, 3D windows, URL mirror) before starting; reviewer notes are kept --no-prefetch do not build subsequent windows in the background --notes-dir PATH <root>/notes; <cache-dir>/notes for a URL root directory for reviewer notes --no-notes do not read or write notes --author NAME your login name author recorded on new notes --open, -v open a browser automatically; enable debug logging

No authentication

Anyone who can reach the port can read the root and write notes. Keep the viewer bound to 127.0.0.1 and connect through an SSH tunnel, or pass --no-notes before binding to 0.0.0.0. On a machine shared with other users, use --uds, as local users can access loopback ports.

docs.title: On the CTU RCI cluster
docs.text:
The viewer can run as a Slurm job on a compute node next to the data, with an SSH tunnel forwarding the interface to your laptop.

  1. On the login node, from the repository root, with .venv-viewer built:

    mkdir -p slurm/slurm_out
sbatch slurm/viewer.batch /mnt/personal/$USER/HELHEST_v2_4    # 8 h

  2. On your laptop:

    scripts/viewer_connect.sh     # [local_port=8080] [job_id]; newest viewer job by default

    It needs ssh access to the login node and runs from a checkout on your laptop. It reads these environment variables:

    Variable Default Meaning VIEWER_USER $USER your RCI account name VIEWER_LOGIN login3.rci.cvut.cz login node VIEWER_REPO /home/$VIEWER_USER/projects/dataset_tools the checkout on the cluster the job was submitted from VIEWER_KNOWN_HOSTS ~/.ssh/known_hosts_rci_nodes known-hosts file for the compute nodes VIEWER_COMPRESS 1 compress the tunnel: a 3D window is ~37 MB raw, ~13 MB compressed; 0 is faster on wired gigabit

    This locates the job's compute node and socket, keeping the tunnel open until you press Ctrl-C. The viewer runs until the Slurm job walltime expires.

  3. Open http://127.0.0.1:8080/.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
URL Shows / one card per scene, filterable by validation status, note verdict, and split (filters are linkable: ?status=, ?verdict=, ?split=) /segments every ground-truth segment with a viewable window in one table /notes all reviewer notes, downloadable as CSV /scene/<id> ground-truth timeline, file inventory, map, extraction/disk/validation cards, signals, and 3D windows /scene/<id>/segment/<n> one ground-truth segment: robot activity, map, notes, and frames /scene/<id>/frame/<n> image, height map, validity mask, a top-down cloud render, and lidar projection onto the camera image /view/<scene>/<window> interactive 3D view: Space plays and pauses; [ and ] step to the previous and next window

A 3D view never spans two segments because each segment has its own coordinate origin. The first time a window is opened, its 3D assets are built; afterwards they load from the cache.

docs.title: Optional root files
docs.text:
Each of these optional files adds information to the pages when present and is re-read automatically when modified:

File Shows as Made by validation.csv, validation.json status chips on the index, scene page Validation card helhest-validate disk_usage.json sizes and disk bars helhest-extract, helhest-disk-usage manifest.json, splits.json, keyframes*.lst dataset version, train/validation split tags and filters helhest-release atlas/ index page's curated header and thumbnails scripts/make_atlas.py notes/ reviewer notes on scenes and frame ranges, with verdicts (keep, drop, fix) the viewer

The viewer automatically detects re-extracted scenes. The --clear-cache flag is only needed if the cache becomes corrupted.
